To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the production of highly charged ions has been demonstrated at the GANIL laboratory.

we are able to produce radioactive beams with high intensity, metallic ions with high charge state and highly charged ions with high charge and low emittance, and that we have demonstrated the feasibility of the production of highly charged ions from a gas target.

we have: (i) developed an ion source for the production of radioactive beams with intensities of the order of 10 ^{8} ions/s, (ii) developed an ion-source for the production of highly charged ions with intensities of 10 ^{10} ions/s, and (iii) developed an ion beam production system for the production of metallic ions with intensities that are one order of magnitude higher than those obtained previously with other ion sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of high quality ion beams, and the development and improvement of the ion sources.

the development of the SPIRAL2 facility for the production of high intensity beams of radioactive ions; the production of high current beams of highly charged metal ions; and the production of intense beams of highly charged ions.

we have developed and are developing new ion sources that will be used for the new radioactive beam facility SPIRAL2, for the new high intensity accelerator project EURISOL and for the high energy physics facility FAIR.
we have developed and implemented several ion sources that have been successfully used for the production of radioactive ion beams, high charge state ions and metallic ion beams.

it is possible to increase the intensities of highly charged ions, which are essential to the production of high-energy radioactive ion beams.
the production of radioactive ion beams is not limited to the production of beams from pure targets, but can be extended to the production from compound targets.
